inputs: .claude/reports/reference-requirements/<reference>.json (13 files, drawer + trigger-close rows, incl. top-level headed_recheck)
reading_notes: Presence is decided by what a visitor sees. away/butcherbox/rabbit/halcyon/indus-foods have NO drawer at 1440 (their desktop menu is the bar + panels); that absence is recorded as its own value in F-C-01, never as a forced fill.

halcyon (6 variants: columns/cards/minimal x light/dark) and indus-foods (2 variants: sectors-cards/sectors-list) record `variant_effect: none` on every drawer cell - the overlay geometry, zone model, mechanics and motion are variant-invariant; only the ground fill and label colour differ, and only on the light/dark axis. Variants are therefore named once per family rather than per cell.
For halcyon and indus-foods the SOURCE and the RENDER disagree on three things and both are recorded separately: entry stagger (F-C-22), Escape-closes (F-C-18) and scroll lock (F-C-19).
resn's drawer text is drawn into per-item canvases; its typography, hover and motion cells are canvas measurements, not DOM computed styles (F-C-10, F-C-12, F-C-21).

butcherbox and rabbit have a `drawer | 768 | present` row with NO cells (`not_measured`: 'the 768 tier was not captured'). They are counted as present at 768 for F-C-01 only and are excluded from every value-bearing family at that tier.

Where headed and headless disagree, the headed value is used: away's headed session is served the UK storefront (12 of 55 static cells differ, 7 of them scrollbar-derived); lusion's and lamalama's pre-intro readings were re-measured headed; resn's 1440 open/close timings and the 768 pointer-block are headed values.

families.name: Drawer presence per tier
families.description: Whether a visitor can open a drawer at all at a given viewport width. Five of the thirteen references have a drawer only below desktop: at 1440 the bar plus its dropdown or mega panels IS the menu and the burger is display:none, so there is nothing a visitor could open.

needed_by.cell: drawer/archetype (1440 = absent, '#mobile-menu is in the DOM but its hamburger is display none (0x0)')
drawer/archetype (1440 = absent, 'visibility hidden, opacity 0, display none at 1440')

sgs_coverage.how_checked: plugins/sgs-blocks/src/blocks/nav-bar-menu/block.json::attributes.collapsePoint (number, default 768) + attributes.showBurger (boolean, default true); DB row `sgs/nav-bar-menu collapsePoint max-width,min-width`, query: sgs-db.py sql "SELECT block_slug, attr_name, css_property FROM block_attributes WHERE block_slug='sgs/nav-bar-menu' AND attr_name IN ('collapsePoint','showBurger')"
sgs_coverage.note: collapsePoint is one width, so 'drawer below N, bar above N' is expressible. A reference that keeps a drawer at EVERY tier (8 of 13) is served by showBurger:true with no collapse.

resn (all tiers, an absolutely positioned route page)

needed_by.cell: drawer/geometry (menu z 995 over backLayer z 990 under curtain z 999)
drawer/archetype + drawer/tier_delta (the archetype CHANGES between tiers: full-width-below-header at 375, side drawer at 768)

sgs_coverage.how_checked: plugins/sgs-blocks/src/blocks/nav-drawer/render.php::$sgs_nd_allowed_anchors = array('full-screen','header','trigger','centred') and render.php::$sgs_nd_geometry_for_anchor (the closure emitting the per-anchor CSS); block.json::attributes.anchor (object, per-device) and attributes.panelSize (object, per-device, consulted only by trigger/centred). DB: sgs-db.py sql "SELECT attr_name, css_property, css_element FROM block_attributes WHERE block_slug='sgs/nav-drawer' AND attr_name IN ('anchor','panelSize')" -> anchor/max-width/dialog, panelSize/NULL.
sgs_coverage.gap: The SIDE DRAWER is missing: there is no anchor that pins the panel to one viewport EDGE at full height with a partial width (away @768: left 0, top 0, 390x900). `trigger` is a top-right corner card with 16px insets and a fit-content height; `header` is full-width. away @768 cannot be expressed. lusion's CONTAINER-WIDE card stack (left/right insets equal to the header container's own insets, not the viewport's) is also not an anchor - `header` gives full-bleed width with no inset - though it is reachable by putting the inner content in an sgs/container with the matching padding.

spec38.tier_V: 9 of 11 measured effects. This scene is page-wide, is a 3D mesh with refraction, and every route sits on it. It returns as a Bean trim/exclude decision under the W4-c termination rule.
spec38.named_FRs: FR-38-19 (page transitions as cross-document View Transitions, Tier V) is the nearest named FR to resn's in-canvas route change and does NOT cover it - an in-canvas single-page transition has no DOM to transition. FR-38-10 SplitText and FR-38-11 ScrambleText (Tier G) are the nearest named FRs to resn's per-item canvas dissolve and are a different look; the digest's own judgement is that the dissolve is expressible in principle as a NEW Tier V canvas-2D effect (the substrate already exists - FR-38-32 particle trail, FR-38-33 grid-dot field) provided the DOM text is kept. unclustered.why: Link labels, promo headlines and social-item names are the site's own copy, not a capability. A family keyed on them would be keyed on prose, which the brief forbids. The one thing in these cells that IS typed - caseOrigin, whether the upper-casing comes from the source text or from CSS text-transform - is clustered into F-C-10.

buck picks its drawer fill from a brand palette PER PAGE LOAD, not per tier (this run gave #196efa / #f4c054 / #508054 at 1440 / 768 / 375; the 2026-07-28 record saw #7f4c1e and #00513c). That is randomised content behaviour, not a styling capability, and clustering it would invent a 'random fill' family that exactly one reference needs and no block attribute should have.

unclustered.cell: drawer/geometry z-index (studionamma 3, wearecollins 1, fantasy 9, lamalama 20, halcyon/indus 300, dogstudio 995, buck 1300, butcherbox 10000)
unclustered.why: An 8-value spread with no design meaning - each is whatever that site's own stacking context required. SGS puts the drawer in the native `<dialog>` top layer, which makes the number irrelevant rather than unmatched. Recorded here so the spread is not mistaken for a missing capability.

unclustered.cell: drawer/geometry.asideRect overshoot (fantasy +100px top and bottom; wearecollins bottom -639 in the 2026-07-28 record)
unclustered.why: An implementation artefact of how those sites size their overlay, not a visible property: the INNER panel is exactly the viewport in both cases, and that is what a visitor sees. Clustering it would create a family keyed on a number no design decision produced.

The labels are drawn into per-item canvases 108x47 / 92x47 / 146x47 with NO DOM text at that tier, so there is no font size, weight or colour to cluster. At 768 and 1440 a hidden DOM copy exists at opacity 0 and those values ARE clustered into F-C-10. A canvas-only label is also something SGS must not reproduce (it deletes real text), so it is a Bean trim/exclude decision under W4-c, not a family.

Both files carry a `drawer | 768 | present` row with no cells and a not_measured entry: 'the 768 tier was not captured for this reference; the emulated viewport pass covered 375 and 1440 only.' Presence is honest, so those rows feed F-C-01; every value-bearing family excludes them at 768 rather than inferring from 375.

A full-size .hover-blocker with pointer-events:none under the items, and a z-index 1005 canvas that intercepts real pointer input at 768 and 375 (reproduced headed on a desktop pointer; iPad and iPhone user agents work by touch). This is a defect in the reference, not a capability any block should express. It is recorded inside F-C-12 and F-C-18 as the reason those cells read the way they do, but it is not a family of its own.

The headed session is served the UK storefront (GBP, /en-gb, the first two nav items swapped, no consent banner) while the JSON describes the US storefront the headless run received; 12 of 55 static cells differ, 7 of them from the 15px classic scrollbar alone. Structure is identical, so every family uses the away values as captured, but WHICH storefront is the reference is an open decision (the file's own follow_up: 'decide which storefront is the reference before Wave 4') and cannot be clustered.
